intro: You are at Cremna, in Burdur province, a city whose story begins in the 3rd century BC. This Roman colony in Pisidia is ringed by cliffs, and here you can still trace the siege ramp and camp the Romans built to put down the revolt of AD 278.
history: This Pisidian city ringed by cliffs was founded in the third century BC, and in 25 BC Augustus made it a Roman colony. Then, in AD 278, a rebel named Lydius seized it. How do you take a town protected by cliffs? The Romans heaped an enormous earth ramp against it to break the siege. That ramp, and the siege camp with it, can still be traced on the ground.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman siege ramp, the forum and basilica, the bath building and the city walls.
facts: Did you know? Kremna is one of the few places in the world where a Roman siege survives whole in the landscape: ramp, camp and walls can all be seen at once. The siege ramp and camp the Romans raised to put down the revolt of AD 278 can still be traced on the ground.
outro: This brings our journey through Cremna to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this landscape keep its story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
